label: a
rationale: This is the structural algebra cluster: batch 1 develops groups, actions, free subgroups, and amenability; batch 5 turns group actions into group-algebra modules and representations; batch 9 supplies the categorical language of kernels, cokernels, exactness, and abelian categories. The representation/module and categorical interfaces are the strongest shared checks, and all three batches fit within one group with no cross-batch dependency edge.

label: b
rationale: These two batches form the arithmetic commutative-algebra pair: batch 2 treats Pell norms, units, continued fractions, and generalized Pell orbits, while batch 3 treats Artinian rings, nilpotence, length, Chinese remainders, and local factors. Both require careful handling of rings, quotients, finite decompositions, and integral arithmetic, making a focused two-batch algebraic review coherent.

label: c
rationale: This is the analysis cluster. Batch 4 covers inner-product operators, spectral decomposition, singular values, and matrix inequalities; batch 7 covers Riemann/Lebesgue integration and convergence; batch 8 covers residues, winding, Rouche, harmonic functions, and domains of holomorphy. Their shared analytic concerns are complex scalars, limits, integration, and operator or boundary arguments, so one group can check conventions across the three pages.

label: d
rationale: The two combinatorics batches are kept together because they are the only repeated category and both fit comfortably in one group. Batch 6 develops partitions, generating functions, Burnside, and Polya cycle indices; batch 10 develops pure pairs, forests, path-antipath classes, quotient blockades, and mixing relations. Their common counting, symmetry, graph, and Erdos-Hajnal conventions make this the natural discrete-combinatorics review group.
